text.text_excerpt: It seems that the reviews of the old location were a mixed bag. I'm here to tell you that I am a big fan of the new location. Located in the space that used to house Nacho mama's, Byblos is a very good Mediterranean restaurant. A friend and I decided to give the new location a try and I am glad we did. During lunch the prices were very reasonable and the service and food were great. I decided to try the combination gyro and schwarma platter. It came with two sides and was around $12. Based on the amount of food I received it was a very fair price. The gyro was good, but the schwarma was the best I've ever had. It was very tender and juicy and had a very exotic flavor. My new favorite Mediterranean restaurant! I'm more of a Greek as opposed to Lebanese person when it comes to this type of food and have been having a hard time finding something to suit me. Byblos did it! Their goat cheese and tomato appetizer was FANTASTIC. We got the sampler platter with beef and chicken gyro meat, tchibouli, and hummus was soooooo good. It's a casual enough place that I felt going there after a workout in my gym clothes and there are a few tables outside if that's your preference. I'll be back!

I absolutely deplore walking into a restaurant - in the daytime no less - and hearing loud techno or house music playing. Some may be fine with that that. But no, not me. Not Kit. What I am a fan of here at Byblos is the food. I started out with the Muhumra dip - it was described as a mix of pomegranate syrup, roasted peppers, walnuts, and some other things I can't remember off hand. It arrived, and looked like a raw, formed hamburger with walnuts on top. I'm doing it no justice by describing it that way, but it's what it looked like. The taste, however, was exceptional.
